trial.title: Analysis of Pedicle Screw Accuracy to Plan Using Medtronic Mazor Robotic System

endpoints.measure: Total deviation (mm) from the pre-planned screw entry point
endpoints.description: Total deviation (mm) from the pre-planned screw entry point includes: deviation in angle of insertion in the axial plane (degrees), and deviation in angle of insertion in the sagittal plane (degrees) from an O-arm spin after screw placement.

endpoints.measure: Accuracy assessment for degree of pedicle breach
endpoints.description: The secondary outcome will include traditional accuracy assessment for degree of pedicle breach utilizing the Gertzbein and Robbins classification system.

analysis_trace: Trial identification: NCT05884593 is a single-arm, interventional study evaluating Mazor X robotic system for pedicle screw placement accuracy in thoracolumbar arthrodesis (T2-S1) at Ohio State University Wexner Medical Center. Enrollment: 50 patients. Expected completion: December 2023.

Patient population: Adults ≥18 years with degenerative conditions, spinal deformity, infection, trauma, or neoplastic processes requiring pedicle screw instrumentation. Exclusions include prior instrumentation at the same level, severe comorbidities, pregnancy. Mixed etiology spinal pathology population.

Target mechanism: Mazor X robotic-guidance system provides preoperative planning and intraoperative navigation to improve pedicle screw placement accuracy versus freehand/fluoroscopic techniques. System uses preoperative CT planning with intraoperative O-arm verification.

Endpoint interpretation: Primary endpoint (primary-0) measures total deviation (mm) from pre-planned screw entry point, including axial and sagittal angular deviations. This is a continuous technical accuracy metric measured via O-arm post-placement. Secondary endpoint (secondary-0) assesses pedicle breach using Gertzbein-Robbins classification (Grade A-E), a categorical clinical safety/accuracy measure at 6 weeks.

Evidence review: Retrieved PMC12090060 (Volk et al., 2023) - multicenter study of Mazor X Stealth Edition with 500 screws in 122 patients. Reported mean medial-lateral deviation 1.75±1.36mm and superior-inferior deviation 1.52±1.26mm in pedicle region. 74% of screws had ≤2mm deviation. This provides direct numeric evidence for same device, similar population (degenerative conditions, spondylolisthesis, stenosis), similar measurement approach (screw-to-plan deviation). Evidence_role: direct_numeric.

Evidence review: Retrieved PMC10834206 (Zhao et al., 2023) - Mazor X Stealth for OLIF with pedicle screw placement. Reported screw accuracy using modified Gertzbein-Robbins. Single-position group showed high accuracy rates comparable to prone positioning. Evidence_role: indirect_direction for Gertzbein classification outcomes.

Evidence review: Systematic reviews (Sagepub meta-analysis) indicate robot-assisted screws achieve >90% Grade A accuracy vs 86.4% freehand. Meta-analytic evidence supports robotic superiority for Gertzbein Grade A rates. Evidence_role: indirect_direction.

Evidence matching: Primary endpoint (deviation mm) - Volk et al. uses same Mazor X system, same measurement concept (screw-to-plan deviation), similar population (adults with degenerative spinal conditions). Minor mismatch: Volk measured pedicle region deviation while NCT05884593 specifies entry point deviation; expected correlation high. Numeric_use_allowed: yes with uncertainty adjustment.

Evidence matching: Secondary endpoint (Gertzbein-Robbins) - Multiple studies confirm robotic systems achieve 90-98% clinically acceptable placement (Grade A+B). Gertzbein classification is standardized. Evidence_role: indirect_direction for grade distribution.

Safety analysis: Robotic pedicle screw placement generally associated with low complication rates. Malposition requiring revision typically <2-3%. No specific safety signals identified for Mazor X in retrieved literature. Neurological deficit risk low with Grade A/B placement.

Key risks: 1) Single-arm design without comparator limits interpretability of 'success' threshold. 2) Expected completion December 2023 but no results posted as of knowledge cutoff - risk of delay/data unavailability. 3) Mixed pathology population may increase variability. 4) Entry point deviation vs pedicle region deviation measurement differences.

Evidence to prediction: For primary-0, based on Volk et al. mean deviation ~1.5-1.8mm with SD ~1.3mm, predict mean total deviation 2.0-2.5mm (accounting for entry point vs pedicle region difference). For secondary-0, predict >90% Grade A, >98% Grade A+B based on meta-analytic patterns.

Coverage gaps: No direct results from NCT05884593 available. No Ohio State-specific published data found. Single-arm design precludes comparative efficacy claims. Long-term clinical outcomes (pain, function) not assessed in this trial.

Confidence assessment: Primary endpoint prediction confidence moderate (0.60) due to strong mechanistic/device-specific evidence but lack of exact endpoint match. Secondary endpoint confidence moderate-high (0.70) due to standardized classification and consistent literature patterns.

analysis_trace: Evidence analysis: (1) Wang et al. 2023 case series (12 patients, 60 screws) using Mazor X showed 98.3% screws within Gertzbein-Robbins safe zone (Grade A+B) - evidence_role: direct_numeric for secondary endpoint, mismatch: smaller sample size, specific population. (2) Oppermann et al. 2023 cadaveric study with Mazor X showed mean deviation 0.9mm (O-arm) vs 1.7mm (preopCT/C-arm) - evidence_role: indirect_direction for primary endpoint, mismatch: cadaveric vs clinical population, different anatomy/soft tissue factors. (3) General robotic spine surgery literature shows mean entry point deviation ~2.0±1.2mm, axial angle 2.2°±1.7°, sagittal angle 2.9°±2.4° - evidence_role: indirect_direction, mismatch: mixed robotic systems, not Mazor X specific. Primary endpoint predicted mean deviation ~1.8mm based on O-arm use (superior accuracy). Secondary endpoint predicted ~97% safe zone rate based on Mazor X specific data. Main uncertainty: limited Mazor X clinical studies with exact deviation measurements; single-arm design without comparator.
